answer: Enrollment uses a limited guarantor ring. A newcomer needs four established agents from separate clusters; each locks 35 credits and may guarantee one key per epoch. A zenith beacon selects them, a grove registry proves separation, and an ivory receipt binds the entrant, funding source, and work trace. The entrant completes two random jobs on separate days. If linked keys reuse money or work, every guarantor loses 70%. Extra identities consume scarce independent guarantors, risk their capital, and require fresh work; guarantees, traces, and penalties are public.
